cards.title: Query fan-out: optimize for the sub-queries AI actually runs
cards.summary: AI assistants expand one user prompt into several background searches, so visibility depends on ranking for those sub-queries, not the original prompt.
cards.use_when: Planning which product, category and landing pages to build or optimize so an AI assistant can surface the store for high-intent shopping prompts.
steps: Understand the mechanism: when someone searches in ChatGPT or Perplexity, the tool 'fans out' the single query into multiple background variations — e.g. 'best running shoes' becomes 'best running shoes 2026'.

Treat this as an SEO problem, not a content-volume problem: AI tools retrieve URLs through search engine APIs (Google, Bing, etc.), so pages that rank in traditional search are the ones eligible for retrieval.

For each commercially important prompt in your catalog (e.g. 'best bathroom vanities', 'best fragrance for men'), list the likely fan-out variations and check whether any page on your site — category page, product page, comparison page — genuinely answers them.
Prioritize building or optimizing the page that serves the fan-out variant with the clearest purchase intent, rather than producing a new article for every variant.
Re-check fan-out behavior periodically, since the assistant's background searches change over time.
caveats: Presented as the source's model of how assistants retrieve pages; the exact search back-end is debated and changes often.
Fan-out behavior is not fully transparent — treat any list of sub-queries as a hypothesis to test, not a fixed map.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Why scaled AI content is a rank-and-tank risk
cards.summary: Mass-producing AI articles to chase fan-out variations creates a short traffic spike followed by a collapse, and the source argues recovery can take years.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to accept a vendor's or in-house plan to scale the store's blog from hundreds to thousands of posts for AI visibility.
steps: Recognize the pattern before committing: the most-promoted GEO method is simply publishing far more content targeting fan-out keyword variations, often via automated content generators.
Anticipate the cycle — the source describes sites going from ~100 to 1,000+ posts in weeks, seeing an initial traffic lift, then declining sharply ('Mount AI' / 'rank and tank').
Weigh the downside as asymmetric: the source states Google already names this 'scaled content abuse' in its guidelines and that sites penalized in an algorithm update can take years to recover.

Check whether the traffic being generated is commercial. The source's critique is that most scaled how-to/what-is/explainer content does not generate revenue — it is top-of-funnel volume for its own sake.
If someone proposes the tactic, ask what happens to the store's core product and category pages in the next algorithm update, not just what the traffic chart looks like today.
caveats: This is the source's strong opinion; recovery timelines cited (2–3 years, 'many case studies') are illustrative, not a guaranteed benchmark.
Brands with strong existing brand search and media mentions may sustain the tactic longer before decline, per the source — that is an observation, not a safe strategy.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Audit a scaled-content case study with keyword difficulty
cards.summary: Aggregate traffic charts can hide a decline in the hard, commercially valuable keywords, so analyze difficulty bands separately.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a GEO agency's or tool's case study before signing, or auditing whether your own scaled content push is actually holding up.
steps: Do not accept the headline traffic chart as proof. The source describes a large finance company whose overall traffic was still above the prior year, appearing to validate the tactic.
Break the case study's keywords into difficulty bands (the source uses Ahrefs difficulty > 30 as the cut) and examine trends separately.

Look for divergence: in the cited example, keywords with difficulty above 30 had begun to decline while easy keywords still propped up the total — meaning the competitive, more useful terms were the first to go.
Ask your own question of any case study: is this traffic producing revenue? If organic or LLM-driven revenue has not increased, the source says it is not a win regardless of the chart.
If you have an SEO tool subscription, verify traffic patterns yourself rather than relying on the vendor's screenshot.
caveats: Difficulty thresholds like 30 are tool-specific heuristics from the source, not universal cut-offs.
A single case example is not evidence the tactic works or fails for every site.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Red flags and yellow flags when vetting a GEO vendor
cards.summary: Screen AI-visibility vendors by whether their platform generates content at scale and by what they actually propose doing off-site.
cards.use_when: Choosing or renewing an agency/tool that promises to improve the store's visibility inside AI assistants.
steps: Biggest red flag: the vendor has a content generator in their platform, or their proposal centers on producing hundreds of blog posts. That is the pattern the source considers the fastest route to a rank-and-tank penalty.
Yellow flag: a Reddit-mentions strategy. Ask specifically how they will post and engage in communities, then verify whether the cited threads are even relevant (see the Reddit verification card).
Demand current performance data on their published case studies: ask the sales rep how the featured client is performing now and how the strategy held up over time.
Ask what they think about off-site SEO (affiliates, third-party listicles) and whether they have a video/YouTube/social strategy, since video appears heavily in Google's AI overviews per the source.
Sanity-test jargon. If they cannot explain their method in plain language you understand, the source treats that as a grifter signal — common across marketing agencies, not just SEO.

Run grifter probes: ask whether they recommend an llms.txt file, a dedicated 'AI info page', or 'chunking' all your content. If they enthusiastically endorse these as necessary, lean toward walking away.
caveats: The llms.txt, AI-info-page and chunking objections are the source's opinion, not established consensus.
An experienced general SEO practitioner may be a better bet than a dedicated GEO vendor, per the source — but verify current tool/format conventions yourself before acting.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: The five questions to ask a GEO vendor before hiring
cards.summary: A concrete question set that surfaces whether an AI-visibility vendor has durable experience or is selling scaled-content tactics.
cards.use_when: Running a sales call or RFP with an agency or platform pitching AI search visibility for your store.
steps: Ask: how do you think GEO is different from SEO? A vague or purely hype-driven answer is a signal.
Ask: how long have you been around, and when did you start in optimization? The source flags companies that appeared only after ChatGPT launched versus those operating in 2015–2017.
Ask: can you share recent case studies — and can you tell me how those clients are performing now and whether the strategy held up?
Ask: what are your thoughts on off-site SEO (affiliate placements, third-party listicles, reviews sites) and on incorporating video and social media into our strategy?
Ask directly: are you going to put up hundreds of blog posts? The source treats a yes as a red flag.
Ask them to explain their approach in plain English; inability to do so is itself disqualifying per the source.
caveats: These are the source's proposed questions; they screen for scaled-content risk, not for every possible vendor weakness.
New vendors are not automatically bad — the source acknowledges newcomers to the industry — but longevity is the screen it recommends.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Correct persistent inaccurate brand facts across public sources
cards.summary: Repeatedly restating a corrected fact on your own site and across distributed channels can shift what a model says even without a web search.
cards.use_when: When an AI assistant keeps repeating an outdated or misleading fact about your store — e.g. shipping times, return policy, product capabilities, implementation or lead times.
steps: Start with your own website: state the corrected fact plainly and explicitly. In the source's example, a company suffering from '9+ months implementation' reputation simply published that implementation can be as fast as 3 weeks. The reasoning: the model repeats information it sees, so your own site is the best place to start.

Distribute the same claim well beyond the website: third-party articles, the founder's social videos addressing the misconception directly, and other channels. The source emphasizes cross-channel repetition, not a single update.

Be realistic about magnitude and lag. LLMs are trained over years, so any single tactic has a minor effect; in the example the model moved from 9+ months to 6 months over roughly two years — an improvement, not the target figure.
Repeat a fixed set of brand questions with browsing controlled where possible; record model, date and cited evidence. Changed answers do not prove retraining.

Treat related off-site profiles as part of the same repair job: G2, Reddit, Trustpilot, local directories and local board-of-trade listings — update them so the stale claim is not being reinforced elsewhere.
caveats: The source says it has seen no true, verifiable case study of a company reliably entering training data through content volume; the demonstrated result here was partial and slow.
Model training cut-offs and behavior change frequently — verify current model behavior rather than assuming a fixed timeline.
The observed SaaS example does not establish control over training data; apply the factual-correction workflow to store policies, specifications and pricing.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Distinguish observed web retrieval from unverified answer provenance
cards.summary: Run the same query in free/incognito and logged-in/paid sessions and inspect citations to see whether the assistant searched the web at all.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in training-data/brand work or web-page optimization for a given set of shopping or brand prompts.
steps: Run an experiment anyone can do: search a prompt in the free version of ChatGPT, then run the same prompt in a separate incognito tab and in a paid/logged-in account, and compare the answers side by side.
Repeat a few times and reword the sentence structure between runs to see how stable the answer is — the source notes answers shift with phrasing.
Check available citations and search or tool traces. Missing citations alone cannot prove that an answer came only from training data.
Prioritize correcting current public product facts and observed cited pages. Label answer provenance unknown when the system does not expose it.
Compare controlled, fresh sessions without supplied brand context where possible; account, memory, model and prompt differences can affect the result.
caveats: Model behavior, paywalls and search triggers change often — re-run the experiment before making decisions.
The source's observations were made at a specific point in time and are not a permanent characterization of any AI product.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Prompt trackers: understand their limits before trusting AI visibility data
cards.summary: Automated AI prompt trackers can report inflated or meaningless visibility when answers vary run-to-run or the model never searched the web.
cards.use_when: Reviewing an AI visibility report from a tool, agency or in-house dashboard to decide whether the store is actually being recommended.
steps: Recognize how these tools work: they capture screenshots of a tracked prompt's answer inside ChatGPT or another assistant and upload them for comparison.
Know the failure mode: if the assistant does not trigger a web search, there are no citations in the answer, so the screen contains no useful evidence of visibility.

Treat citation counts with suspicion. The source argues citations are easy to inflate — one URL can be cited for an infinite number of branded term variations (e.g. 'how to get rid of mold brand name'), so 'we increased citations' does not mean 'we increased visibility'.
Recognize that answers vary dynamically; a single tracked prompt is not a stable measurement.
When reviewing reports, ask which prompts are commercially meaningful to the store, whether web search actually fired, and whether the reported change maps to revenue rather than mention counts.
caveats: The source's view is that the whole citation-measurement system is of questionable value and partly vendor-driven; treat dashboard metrics as directional at best.
Trackers and assistants change interfaces and behavior — verify the current mechanics before relying on any single metric.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Verify claimed Reddit influence before paying for Reddit GEO
cards.summary: Test which Reddit threads actually influence the prompts you care about — often none you can join, and some are locked.
cards.use_when: Being pitched a Reddit-mentions service for your store, or considering building a Reddit presence for AI visibility.
steps: Take the keywords and conversational prompts that matter commercially to the store and run them through an SEO or GEO tool to see the specific Reddit URLs being cited by AI for those prompts.
Identify the subreddits involved and check their rules: the source notes some high-engagement subreddits ban your account the moment a brand name is mentioned, even in a genuinely helpful answer.
Accept dead ends quickly. In the source's example, the only cited Reddit thread for a bathroom-vanity query was eight years old and locked — creating fifty new pages could not break into that answer.

If a vendor claims 'increased Reddit mentions', ask what influence that had on the answers you care about. The source warns that many vendor Reddit posts are autogenerated, add no value, and receive no engagement.
Prefer publishers that already hold AI citations over chasing new Reddit threads that no model currently references.
caveats: Reddit is genuinely cited by AI assistants, per the source, but that does not mean any given Reddit tactic works for any given query.
Subreddit rules and AI citation sources change over time — re-verify which threads are actually referenced.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Get listed in the third-party listicles AI already cites
cards.summary: Find the affiliate review pages and listicles that influence your priority prompts and get your brand placed in those, not in new ones you create.
cards.use_when: Building off-site AI visibility for a store in a category where comparison listicles (supplements, mattresses, credit cards, fragrances, software) drive AI answers.
steps: Use your GEO or SEO tool's 'sources' section to see which third-party URLs influence the AI answers for your priority prompts; these tools typically flag sources where you are not mentioned.
Skip competitor-owned listicles — the source states it will not email a competitor asking to be added, and ignores such requests when received.

Target durable, high-authority publishers in your vertical (the source cites examples like Healthline, WebMD, Sleepopolis for mattresses, large credit-card affiliates) and try to join their affiliate programs, even at a higher cost than you would like.

For smaller or niche blogs that turn out to be influencing many of your prompts, simply email and ask what it would cost to be included — the source describes this as a straightforward paid placement, sometimes very cheap, that can win citations across many prompts.

Run the same analysis on competitors: use link/backlink intersection analysis to see which listicles and guest posts they appear in, then pursue the equivalent for your brand — bigger publications for bigger companies, local or cheaper sites for local players.
Remember the affiliate is often a different team from SEO, so if you run or influence the affiliate program, coordinate with them directly.
caveats: The source notes an unethical variant — companies sponsoring or buying listicles on third-party news sites (it cites a hair-transplant listicle in a Canadian newspaper and law-firm pages) — and explicitly does not recommend or condone it; disclosure requirements vary by industry and jurisdiction.
Affiliate programs sometimes test placement and click-through rate before giving premium positions.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Rank category and product pages for bottom-of-funnel queries without building listicles
cards.summary: Your own category and product pages can capture high-intent queries and get cited by AI, without any third-party placement.
cards.use_when: Deciding what to build next on-site for AI visibility — a new blog post or an optimized commercial page.
steps: Put up product and landing pages that target high-intent terms directly, and cover the use cases and services you offer — the source describes these as being cited heavily in AI answers, and calls the tactic fully ethical.

Use e-commerce category page conventions the source observed: a fragrance site's category page can carry the title and H1 'best fragrances for men' while still presenting the normal product grid — no article required to rank for a bottom-of-funnel query.
Apply the same pattern to service pages: a service page can be optimized for a scenario-driven query rather than written as a blog post.

Use borrowed credibility where it is legitimate: the source describes a law firm that earned a ranking from a legal publication's affiliate program, then published a page citing that recognition, and subsequently appeared for 'best personal injury lawyers in Canada'.

Prioritize commercial pages over explainer content; the source observes many competitive commercial keywords (e.g. 'personal injury law NYC') have surprisingly few sites targeting them properly, despite high cost per click.
caveats: The borrowed-credibility example is a third-party recognition placement; check advertising and endorsement disclosure rules in your industry and market.
SCALE the approach with judgment — the value comes from targeting genuinely searched queries, not from generating pages for their own sake.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Treat GEO as a company-wide function, not a single marketing hire
cards.summary: Because AI answers draw on product quality, reviews, PR, social and support channels, one person cannot fix AI visibility alone.
cards.use_when: Scoping who owns AI search performance at your store and setting cross-team responsibilities.
steps: Map the owners: product quality (bad products generate bad Reddit sentiment regardless of optimization), brand reputation and executive conduct, communications/PR messaging, review profiles (Trustpilot, G2, Glassdoor), affiliate relationships, and web content.

Fix the underlying substance first: if the product or service is genuinely poor, the source is explicit that no amount of Reddit or listicle optimization will overcome what customers say about it publicly.

Align messaging across channels. If the company has been known for one thing for 15 years and wants to be known for something else, a press release alone will not change what AI says — sustained promotion across many channels is required.

Use review profiles as a lever: in the source's example, a law firm improved its Glassdoor rating above four stars by encouraging employee reviews, after which ChatGPT stopped using Glassdoor as its review source. The same logic applies to Trustpilot for consumer brands.
Ensure the affiliate, PR and content owners are coordinate-able, since the cited sources often sit outside SEO's control.
caveats: The Glassdoor example is an anecdote about one firm and one model's source selection at a point in time, not a repeatable guarantee.
Encouraging reviews must comply with platform policies and applicable law; the source mentions incentives without addressing compliance.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Investigate stale brand facts and correct likely public sources
cards.summary: When a model answers about your brand without searching, it is drawing on sources like G2, Reddit or directories — correct those sources directly.
cards.use_when: An AI assistant gives an outdated answer about your store's policies, pricing, product capabilities or review sentiment without performing a web search.
steps: Use matching wording to identify candidate stale sources; wording similarity does not prove training provenance.
Review brand-plus-review and comparison answers; fix inaccurate editable profiles and invite honest customer reviews without screening for positivity.
For local businesses, update directory and local board-of-trade listings — these are the kinds of sources the source names as feeding training data.

Redistribute the corrected claim beyond the profile itself: onto your website, into third-party articles, and into social video from the founder, as in the case study that moved the answer from 9+ months to 6 months.
Retest in controlled fresh sessions with browsing disabled where possible, and record uncertainty about model memory or training effects.
caveats: The source is explicit that it has not seen a truly verifiable case study of a company deliberately entering training data — the demonstrated effect was partial and took roughly two years.
Which sources feed which model is not published and changes over time; treat the G2/Reddit/directory list as the source's working hypothesis.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Test whether an AI answer is naming your brand or only linking your page
cards.summary: A citation is not the same as a mention — being linked while a competitor is named is not a win for the store.
cards.use_when: Reviewing an AI visibility report or checking a Google AI overview for your category to judge whether the visibility claimed is worth anything.
steps: Run your priority queries and read the AI answer carefully. The source describes a case where an AI FP&A software company was cited in Google's AI overview but not named — the answer listed other companies as best and merely linked to their page.
Interpret the two outcomes differently: a mention puts your brand in front of the buyer; a bare link may just position you as a source that recommends rivals.
When a vendor reports growth in 'AI visibility', ask whether it is mentions or citations, and which prompts, before treating it as progress.

Watch for site-scoped searches in the fan-out. The source observed ChatGPT temporarily issuing searches like 'site:G2.com company-name' — evidence that assistants are actively working to improve answer quality and may bypass self-authored listicles.
Use the finding to decide whether to invest in being mentioned inside trusted publishers rather than in publishing your own listicle that names you first.
caveats: The site: operator behavior was observed during a limited window and may have been a test; re-verify current behavior.
Google AI overviews and assistant answers change format often.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx

cards.title: Judge AI-visibility tactics by whether they optimize for the user's best answer
cards.summary: The durable test for any GEO tactic is whether it improves the experience of searchers, not whether it produces a spike in tracked mentions.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to adopt a specific AI-visibility tactic — self-authored listicles, scaled comparison pages, paid placements — for your store.
steps: Apply the source's test question to each tactic: does this give a user who lands on the page through Google or an AI search engine the best possible experience?

Use it to reject the spammy version of a legitimate tactic. Comparison pages have existed in legitimate form for years (mattress brand A vs brand B); the GEO version is scaling them to the point of comparing brands nobody searches for.

Apply the same test to self-authored listicles that place your own company first — they may still rank and be cited, but the source frames them as a tactic that assistants are actively working around.
Prefer the version of the tactic that serves real intent: your own product, category and comparison pages that answer genuine buyer questions (see the bottom-of-funnel page card).
Use it as the tiebreaker when a vendor presents a case study: ask whether the pages in question help buyers or simply exist to capture a fan-out variation.
caveats: This is the source's stated ethical/strategic frame, and it explicitly names some effective-but-unethical tactics it does not recommend.
'Best possible experience' is a judgment call — apply it consistently rather than as a rhetorical test.
cards.source_name: Generative Engine Optimization_ Is It Safe and How to Do It the Right Way.docx
